title: IRON-Meme: A Benchmark for Structured Understanding of Identities and Roles in Online Meme Narratives
abstract: arXiv:2610.33097v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As polarization grows on social media, understanding how political memes shape online narratives has become increasingly important. Previous research has relied on either qualitative frameworks that are hard to scale or computational methods that lack theoretical grounding. Both approaches treat narrative categories in isolation and focus exclusively on moral portrayals of identity. To address these limitations, we introduce a framework grounded in social science theories, encompassing three categories: social identities (such as gender, politics, and ethnicity), viewpoints (ingroup and outgroup perspectives), and narrative roles (moral character, intelligence, status, and power). translated_abstract: 随着社交媒体上极化现象的加剧，理解政治迷因如何塑造网络叙事变得日益重要。以往的研究要么依赖于难以规模化的定性框架，要么采用缺乏理论依据的计算方法。这两种方法都将叙事类别孤立对待，并且仅仅关注身份的道德刻画。为了解决这些局限性，我们提出了一个基于社会科学理论的框架，涵盖三个类别：社会身份（如性别、政治和种族）、观点（内群体和外群体视角）以及叙事角色（道德品质、智力、地位和权力）。基于这一框架，我们构建了IRON-Meme，这是一个由人工标注的基准数据集，包含1,110个政治迷因，其模板数量大大超过现有的基准数据集。我们对IRON-Meme的分析表明，大多数迷因都赋予贬损性角色，并且身份
tldr: 该论文提出了一个基于社会科学理论的叙事框架，涵盖社会身份、观点和叙事角色三大类别，并构建了包含1,110个政治迷因的人工标注基准数据集IRON-Meme，为结构化理解网络迷因叙事中的身份与角色提供了大规模研究资源。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a social-science-grounded framework covering social identities, viewpoints, and narrative roles, and presents IRON-Meme, a human-annotated benchmark of 1,110 political memes across substantially more templates than prior benchmarks, enabling structured understanding of identities and roles in online meme narratives.
